tags.instructions: Use a known Intune managed device ID from your device inventory. Verify reboot support and administrator authority first. The action can interrupt users and unsaved work. This returns request acceptance only; inspect device action history in Intune before retrying an ambiguous result.

functions.name: request-managed-device-check-in
functions.description: Request that one managed device synchronize with Intune. This triggers device check-in; it does not replicate a dataset for the caller.

managedDeviceId.description: Opaque Intune managed device ID to request a check-in for.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_requestma.description: Identifies the managed device for a single check-in request.

id.description: Managed device ID addressed by the check-in request.

accepted.description: Provider accepted the check-in action, not proof that synchronization has finished.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_requestm.description: Acceptance of the device check-in request, without waiting for device communication.

tags.instructions: Use a known Intune managed device ID from your device inventory. This requests a device check-in and returns acceptance, not a completed synchronization or newly refreshed inventory. Inspect status in Intune afterward. Do not use this when you only want to read stored device information.

functions.name: request-managed-device-location
functions.description: Request a location action for one managed device. The result acknowledges the request, not coordinates or a completed location fix.

managedDeviceId.description: Opaque Intune managed device ID whose location to request.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_requestma.description: The managed device for which to request a location action.

id.description: Managed device ID to which the location request was addressed.

accepted.description: Provider accepted the location action; no coordinates or location completion are established.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_requestm.description: Acknowledgment of the location action request, not a device location or completion result.

tags.instructions: Use a known Intune managed device ID from your device inventory, not an app registration ID or directory device ID. You need device-action authority and a device that supports location. This tool returns acceptance only; inspect device action status in Intune afterward. Do not repeat an ambiguous request automatically.

functions.name: reset-managed-device-passcode
functions.description: Request a passcode reset on one managed device. The action does not accept a chosen passcode or return a new passcode.

managedDeviceId.description: Opaque Intune managed device ID whose device passcode to reset.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_resetmana.description: The managed device addressed by the passcode reset request.

id.description: Managed device ID addressed by the passcode reset.

accepted.description: Provider accepted the reset request; no new passcode or completed reset is asserted.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_resetman.description: Acknowledgment of the reset request, not completion or a new passcode.

tags.instructions: Use a known Intune managed device ID from your inventory. This affects device access and requires supported management mode and passcode-reset authority. It does not reset an app PIN or directory account password. Inspect action status and any recovery information in Intune afterward; do not replay an ambiguous reset automatically.

functions.name: retire-managed-device
functions.description: Request retirement of one managed device from organizational management. This is distinct from a full device wipe; exact platform-specific removal effects require validation.

managedDeviceId.description: Opaque Intune managed device ID to retire from organizational management.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_retireman.description: The managed device to request retirement for.

id.description: Managed device ID addressed by the retirement request.

accepted.description: Provider accepted retirement, not proof of device-side data removal or completed unenrollment.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_retirema.description: Acceptance of the retirement request, without waiting for device-side completion.

tags.instructions: Use a known Intune managed device ID from your inventory. Retirement can remove organizational management and data and is not merely deleting an inventory row. Use `wipe-managed-device` only when a device wipe is intended. No undo is promised. This returns request acceptance; check device action history in Intune before retrying.

functions.name: scan-managed-device-with-windows-defender
functions.description: Request a quick or full Windows Defender scan on one managed device. Success acknowledges the scan request, not a clean-device verdict.

scanType.description: Requested scan depth; defaults to full, corresponding to quickScan=false.

managedDeviceId.description: Opaque Intune managed device ID to scan.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_scanmanag.description: Managed device and requested Windows Defender scan depth.

id.description: Managed device ID addressed by the scan request.

accepted.description: Provider accepted the scan action; not scan completion or absence of malware.

scanType.description: Effective requested scan type, including the local default.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_scanmana.description: Acknowledgment of the submitted Windows Defender scan request, not a scan result.

tags.instructions: Use a known Intune managed device ID for a device supporting Windows Defender scans. Select quick or full; the default is full, which may consume substantial device resources. The tool only submits the action and returns within two minutes; inspect scan results and action history in Intune afterward.

functions.name: update-device-category
functions.description: Partially update category metadata while preserving identity and omitted fields; requires category administration authority.

description.description: Replacement description; omitted preserves, null clears, empty stores empty text.

displayName.description: Replacement name; omitted preserves existing, null and empty rejected.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_updatedev.description: A category ID and at least one replacement metadata field.

id.description: Unchanged category ID.

description.description: Stored description after update; null and empty retained, absent omitted.

displayName.description: Stored name after update; omitted if absent.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_updatede.description: Stored category metadata returned after the update.

tags.instructions: Find ID using `list-device-categories` or `get-device-category`. Supply only changed fields. Null clears description; omission preserves it. Use `delete-device-category` for removal.

functions.name: update-device-compliance-policy
functions.description: Partially modify policy metadata or concrete settings, preserving identity and omitted settings. Requires policy administration authority and may change enforcement on assigned devices.

settings.description: Only concrete setting keys to change; omitted keys preserved. Supplied nested objects/arrays replace the setting; null clears nullable settings, [] empties arrays. Metadata, type, navigation and read-only fields forbidden.

description.description: Replacement description; omission preserves, null clears, empty stores empty text.

displayName.description: Replacement name; omission preserves, null and empty rejected.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_updatedev.description: Partial changes to one device compliance policy, preserving omitted metadata and settings.

id.description: Unchanged policy ID.

updated.description: Provider acknowledged update, not device enforcement completion.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_updatede.description: Acknowledgement of a device compliance policy update, not device enforcement completion.

tags.instructions: Get ID/current definition with `get-device-compliance-policy`. Supply only changed metadata and setting keys. Supplied nested settings replace that setting in full, not recursively merge. This does not alter assignments or schedules. Check current definition before retrying uncertain writes.

functions.name: update-device-compliance-policy-assignments
functions.description: Replace the deployment target set for one device compliance policy. Empty targets clears its assignments.

type.description: Group inclusion, group exclusion, all licensed users, or all devices.

groupId.description: Opaque directory group ID, required only for group and exclusionGroup.

items.description: One audience to include in or exclude from policy deployment.

targets.description: Complete desired target set; at most 100, with an empty array requesting removal of all assignments.

deviceCompliancePolicyId.description: Opaque device compliance policy ID in this tenant.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_updatedev.description: Device compliance policy and its complete desired deployment target set.

id.description: Policy ID whose assignment replacement was accepted.

accepted.description: The provider accepted the assignment action; no device compliance or per-target completion is asserted.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_updatede.description: Acceptance of the assignment action, without asserting device evaluation or per-target completion.

tags.instructions: You need the device compliance policy ID and any directory group IDs from your policy inventory or administrator. Supply the entire desired target set, up to 100 targets: omitted existing assignments are removed, and [] clears all. This changes policy deployment, not the policy's compliance rules or observed device compliance.

functions.name: update-device-configuration
functions.description: Partially modify profile metadata/settings, requiring configuration administration authority. Edits can change assigned-device behavior.

settings.description: Concrete keys to change; omitted keys preserved. Supplied nested values replace the setting; null clears nullable settings, [] empties arrays. Metadata/type/navigation/read-only keys forbidden.

description.description: Replacement description; omitted preserves, null clears, empty stores empty text.

displayName.description: Replacement name; omitted preserves, null and empty rejected.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_updatedev.description: Changes to an existing device configuration, leaving omitted metadata and settings unchanged.

id.description: Unchanged configuration ID.

updated.description: Provider acknowledged change, not installation completion.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_updatede.description: Acknowledgement that the provider updated the configuration, not that devices installed it.

tags.instructions: Get ID/current settings using `get-device-configuration`. Supply only changed fields/keys. A supplied nested setting replaces that setting in full, not recursively merge. This does not alter assignments. Use `delete-device-configuration` for removal.

functions.name: update-device-configuration-assignments
functions.description: Replace the deployment target set for one device configuration. An empty target set clears its assignments.

deviceConfigurationId.description: Opaque device configuration ID in this tenant.

type.description: Group inclusion, group exclusion, all licensed users, or all devices.

groupId.description: Opaque directory group ID, required only for group or exclusionGroup.

items.description: One deployment audience, including a directory group ID only for group inclusion or exclusion.

targets.description: Complete desired assignment target set, at most 100; an empty array removes all assignments.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_updatedev.description: The device configuration and its complete desired deployment target set.

id.description: Configuration ID whose assignment replacement was accepted.

accepted.description: Provider accepted the assignment action, not device-side application or per-target completion.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_updatede.description: Acknowledgment that the provider accepted the configuration assignment action.

tags.instructions: You need a device configuration ID and directory group IDs from your configuration inventory or administrator. Supply the entire desired target set, up to 100 targets; omitted existing targets are removed, and [] clears all. This changes deployment, not the settings inside the configuration or proof of application on devices.

functions.name: update-managed-device
functions.description: Partially update a managed device's administrative friendly name, IT notes, or ownership classification without replacing its inventory.

managedDeviceId.description: Opaque Intune managed-device ID to update.

managedDeviceName.description: Administrative friendly name; omit to preserve, null to clear, or empty string to set empty text. Does not rename the device OS.

notes.description: IT administrator notes as ordinary Unicode text; omit to preserve, null to clear, or empty string to set empty text.

ownerType.description: Intune ownership classification to assign; omit to preserve. Null and empty values are not accepted.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_updateman.description: The managed device to update and only the administrative properties to change; supply at least one editable property.

id.description: Intune managed-device ID addressed by the successful update.

updated.description: The provider acknowledged the administrative update; not a claim that the physical device has checked in.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_updatema.description: Acknowledgement that Intune accepted the administrative update for the addressed managed device.

tags.instructions: Obtain the Intune ID from `list-managed-devices` and inspect current administrative values with `get-managed-device`. Supply only fields to change; null clears notes or the friendly name, while an empty string sets empty text. This changes Intune administrative metadata, not the physical device's reported name, and does not wipe or retire it. Verify uncertain outcomes with `get-managed-device` before repeating a write.

functions.name: update-mobile-app
functions.description: Partially modify an existing catalog app's common metadata without changing its assignments.

mobileAppId.description: Opaque catalog mobile app ID in this tenant.

notes.description: New administrator notes; null clears, empty text sets empty notes.

owner.description: New owner text; null requests clearing.

developer.description: New developer text; null requests clearing.

publisher.description: New publisher text; null requests clearing.

isFeatured.description: New featured status; false explicitly removes featured status.

description.description: New description; null clears and empty text sets an empty description.

displayName.description: New app title; null requests clearing, subject to provider validation.

informationUrl.description: New more-information URL text; null clears.

privacyInformationUrl.description: New privacy statement URL text; null clears.

changes.description: Partial metadata changes; omitted properties stay unchanged, null clears a nullable value, and empty strings are explicit empty text.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_updatemob.description: Identify an existing catalog app and supply only its common metadata changes.

id.description: ID of the app whose metadata change was accepted.

accepted.description: The provider accepted the metadata update; does not establish publication or device installation.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_updatemo.description: Acknowledgment that the provider accepted the requested app metadata update.

tags.instructions: Use an ID from `list-mobile-apps` or `get-mobile-app`. Send only fields to change; null clears a nullable field and empty text sets empty text. Use `update-mobile-app-assignments` for deployment changes and `delete-mobile-app` to remove the entry.

functions.name: update-mobile-app-assignments
functions.description: Replace a mobile app's deployment assignment set with explicit targets and installation intents. Omitted existing targets are removed; an empty set removes all assignments.

intent.description: Deployment intent: optional installation, required installation, requested uninstall, or availability without enrollment.

type.description: Group inclusion, group exclusion, all licensed users, or all devices.

groupId.description: Directory group ID, required only for group and exclusionGroup.

target.description: Audience to include or exclude; directory group IDs must already be known.

items.description: One target and its desired deployment intent.

assignments.description: Complete desired assignment set, at most 100; empty removes all. Existing per-assignment settings are replaced by provider defaults unless the provider preserves them.

mobileAppId.description: Opaque catalog app ID whose deployment assignment set to replace.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_updatemob.description: App and complete desired deployment assignment set.

id.description: App ID whose assignment replacement was accepted.

accepted.description: Provider accepted the assignment request; no per-target or device-side completion is asserted.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_updatemo.description: Acceptance of the assignment request, not device deployment completion.

tags.instructions: Obtain the app ID from `list-mobile-apps` and review every current assignment page with `list-mobile-app-assignments` first. Supply the entire desired assignment set, up to 100 entries; omitted assignments are removed and [] clears all. Group IDs must already be known directory group IDs. An uninstall intent requests device-side removal. Success is acceptance, not installation completion.

functions.name: wipe-managed-device
functions.description: Request a device wipe with explicit data, enrollment, eSIM retention, and optional macOS unlock choices. This can erase user data and has no promised undo.

keepUserData.description: Request retention of user data where supported; defaults to false. Platform prerequisites and compatible combinations must be checked.

macOsUnlockCode.description: Optional macOS unlock code required for the applicable wipe workflow; preserve it as text, including leading zeroes. Omit for non-macOS devices.

managedDeviceId.description: Opaque Intune managed device ID to wipe.

keepEnrollmentData.description: Request retention of enrollment data where supported; defaults to false.

persistEsimDataPlan.description: Request persistence of the eSIM data plan where supported; defaults to false.

FunctionInput_microsoft_intune_wipemanag.description: Target managed device and explicit platform-dependent wipe retention and unlock choices.

id.description: Managed device ID addressed by the wipe request.

accepted.description: Provider accepted the wipe request; not proof that erasure completed or retention succeeded.

FunctionOutput_microsoft_intune_wipemana.description: Acknowledgment of the wipe request, not confirmation that the device was erased.

tags.instructions: Use a known Intune managed device ID and verify its platform and wipe support with your administrator. Defaults retain neither user data, enrollment data, nor eSIM plans. Retention flags are platform-dependent requests, not universal guarantees. Use `retire-managed-device` for organizational retirement instead. This returns acceptance only; check action history before retrying, as another wipe can be harmful.
